# BusViewer

`busviewer` (app id `dev.mixos.busviewer`) is a native window onto the Bus
of the node it runs on. It asks noded which services are registered, asks
each service to describe its verbs, and shows them as a tree. Select a verb
to read its arguments and description, type a JSON body, and call it. The
reply is shown with its return code. BusViewer also lists the mesh nodes
this node can see.

It is for people and agents who want to see what a node offers and try a
verb by hand. It ships in the `mixos-desktop` package set. Nothing else in
the workspace depends on it.

BusViewer is also the reference app for driving a window over the Bus.
Everything in its window is a Bus verb, and
[Driving apps over the Bus](../docs/drive.md#busviewer-the-worked-example)
uses it as the worked example.

The source is
[`apps/busviewer`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/apps/busviewer).

## How it is built

BusViewer follows the engine-first rule in
[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/AGENTS.md) §4.1. It is
two crates:

- **`inspector`** (`crates/inspector`): the headless engine. No UI and no
  I/O. It holds the protocol model, the discovery and call rules, and the
  handling of every `busviewer.*` verb.
- **`busviewer`**: the egui shell. It draws the engine's state, runs the
  engine's effects on a small tokio runtime, and owns the command registry
  that the menus, the shortcuts and the Bus all go through.

The engine never does work itself. The shell feeds it events (Bus
deliveries, finished discoveries and calls, edits made in the window), and
the engine returns `Effect`s for the shell to carry out: `Discover`,
`Call`, `Show`, `Reply`, `Commands`, `Execute`, `Describe`, `Drive`, `Copy`
and `Exit`. Every effect that leaves the process carries a ticket. A
completion whose ticket is not the one in flight is ignored, so a late
reply can never land on a newer operation.

### inspector

| Module | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `model` | `Verb`, `Snapshot` (services, each with its verbs or an error; peers), `Selection`, the parsers for `noded.list`, `noded.peers`, `HELP` and `app.describe`, the limits, and `describe()`, the app's own verb list |
| `engine` | `Engine`, `Effect`, `Dialog`, `Row` and `RowKind` (the services tree), `UiState` (what a person arranges), `Session` (the session theme) |
| `bus` | the connection, through the shared [citizen](../citizen/README.md) library: `start`, `probe`, `forward`, `show`, and `discover` |

Discovery calls `noded.list` and `noded.peers`, then asks every service for
`HELP`, falling back to `app.describe`. It describes eight services at a
time. A service that fails to describe itself shows as an error row and
does not stop the others.

The limits are fixed in `model`:

- a JSON body is at most 65,536 bytes;
- a reply is shown up to 1,000,000 bytes, then marked as truncated.

### busviewer

| Module | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `src/main.rs` | options, single-instance launch, the eframe window |
| `src/lib.rs` | the string catalogue: `strings()`, `label()`, `label_with()` |
| `src/shell.rs` | `Shell`: applies events, settles effects, runs Bus work, follows the desktop profile, wires the toolkit drive layer |
| `src/view.rs` | `view()`: draws the engine's state and returns what the person did as `UiEvent`s; it never changes state itself |
| `src/commands.rs` | `registry()`: every command, with its menu, shortcut, icon and when it is enabled |
| `i18n/en/busviewer.ftl` | the English strings |

The shell applies one event and settles its effects before it reads the
next, so a later delivery can never change what an earlier command acts
on. Within one frame, edits are applied before commands, so a call uses
the body the person sees. Bus work wakes the window only when something
finished; nothing polls.

## Rules

- **One operation at a time.** A refresh or a call in flight makes the
  window busy. Bus requests that need it idle are refused with `BUSY`.
- **A call is sent once.** BusViewer never retries. A transport failure is
  reported as return code 10 with the outcome unknown.
- **No call on bad input.** An unadvertised target, a body over the limit
  or invalid JSON is refused before anything is sent. An empty body is
  allowed.
- **Closing answers everything.** Quit waits until accepted work is
  finished, and every Bus request already accepted gets an answer before
  the connection stops.
- **One window per session.** A second launch finds the running BusViewer
  on the Bus, asks it to show its window through compd, and exits.

## Bus

BusViewer registers as `busviewer` on the local broker. Its verbs are
registered in
[`verbs.conf.mix`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/docs/docs/spec/bus/verbs.conf.mix)
with owner `busviewer`.

- Reading: `busviewer.ping`, `busviewer.info`, `busviewer.tree`,
  `busviewer.reply`, `busviewer.commands`, plus `HELP` and `app.describe`.
- Changing state: `busviewer.filter`, `busviewer.expand`,
  `busviewer.select_row`, `busviewer.select`, `busviewer.body`,
  `busviewer.split`, `busviewer.dialog`, `busviewer.theme`,
  `busviewer.call`, `busviewer.execute`, `busviewer.refresh`,
  `busviewer.show`, `busviewer.quit`.
- The window's drive verbs, from the toolkit: `busviewer.ui.tree`,
  `busviewer.ui.click`, `busviewer.ui.pointer`, `busviewer.ui.scroll`,
  `busviewer.ui.key`, `busviewer.ui.type`, `busviewer.ui.menu`,
  `busviewer.ui.menu.list`, `busviewer.ui.menu.open`,
  `busviewer.ui.menu.close`, `busviewer.ui.capture`, `busviewer.window`
  and `busviewer.window.state`.

Arguments, answers and refusal codes (`BUSY`, `DISCONNECTED`, `ARGUMENT`,
`UNKNOWN_VERB`, `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, `DISABLED`) are tabled in
[Driving apps over the Bus](../docs/drive.md#busviewer-the-worked-example).
Tree rows are named by key, for example `service:noded` or
`verb:noded:noded.list`.

Calling a verb from Mix through BusViewer:

```mix
$body = json_encode({service: "noded", verb: "noded.list"})
send busviewer busviewer.call body=$body timeout=30
print $result
```

The answer is `{service, verb, request_body, rc, body}`.

## Commands and keys

Every menu item, shortcut and `busviewer.execute` id is one command in
`src/commands.rs`:

| Command | Menu | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `file.refresh` | File › Refresh services | Ctrl+R |
| `file.quit` | File › Quit | Ctrl+Q |
| `edit.format` | Edit › Format JSON body | Ctrl+Shift+F |
| `edit.clear` | Edit › Clear body | |
| `edit.copy` | Edit › Copy reply | |
| `bus.call` | Bus › Call verb | Ctrl+Enter |
| `help.shortcuts` | Help › Keyboard shortcuts | F1 |
| `help.about` | Help › About BusViewer | |
| `view.search` | title bar search button | Ctrl+F |
| `view.mode` | title bar light/dark button | |

View › Theme adds the `view.theme.*`, `view.mode.*`, `view.style.*`,
`view.decorations.*` and `view.captions.*` choices. They set the theme of
this window only; the session's theme file is never written. The Help menu
opens with a field that searches every command. The desktop profile can
rebind the shortcuts (`keymaps.busviewer.<id>`), and `busviewer.commands`
reports the ones in force.

## Running it

```text
busviewer [--noded-url URL] [--service NAME] [--comp NAME]
```

- `--noded-url`: the broker to use. The default is the session's noded.
- `--service`: the Bus name to register as, `busviewer` by default.
- `--comp`: the compositor's service name, used to raise the window. The
  default is `$MIXOS_COMP_SERVICE`, or `comp`.

Service names may contain only ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`.

The window follows the desktop profile's look and keymaps from
[settingsd](../settingsd/README.md), through the
[settings](../settings/README.md) follower, and updates when they change.
With no theme chosen it starts in Studio Dark.

## Testing

On an authorised build worker at a pushed commit:

```text
cargo test --locked -p inspector -p busviewer
```

- The engine's unit tests (`crates/inspector/src/engine.rs`, `model.rs`)
  cover discovery, selection, the body, calls, the Bus verbs, refusals,
  tickets and quitting, with no UI.
- `tests/shell.rs` runs the real `Shell` on a logging Bus handle (the
  `inspector` `testing` feature) and checks every reply, call and the final
  quit in order.
- `tests/drive.rs` drives the window over its Bus verbs against the real
  view: clicks, typing, the title bar controls, menus.
- `tests/view.rs` checks the dialogs, the body buttons and their tooltips,
  and the search field through kittest.
- `tests/snapshot.rs` takes offscreen snapshots in several themes into
  `tests/snapshots/`. Regenerate with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` and look at the
  images before committing them.
- `tests/registry.rs` checks that the verb registry lists exactly the
  verbs BusViewer describes, and that read-only verbs are class `query`
  ([verb classes](../docs/decisions/2026-10-11-verb-classes.md)).
- `crates/inspector/tests/native.rs` runs discovery, calls and
  single-instance registration against an isolated real broker. It is
  ignored by default and needs `BUSVIEWER_TEST_URL`.

<!-- page: https://mixos.dev/ced/ (source: https://mixos.dev/ced/README.md) -->

# Ced

Ced is the MixOS Editor: a desktop editor over the `edit` Bus service
([editd](../editd/README.md)). A document lives in the service, not in the
window, so several people and agents can edit it at once. Ced shows their
carets, selections and changes as they happen, and keeps typing instant by
applying it locally first.

## Running

```
ced [PATH[:LINE[:COL]]…]   open paths (in the running ced, if there is one)
ced --headless             every verb, no window
ced --service NAME         register as NAME (tests)
```

The edit service must be running. Ced registers on the Bus as `ced`; a
second `ced` hands its paths to the first and exits.

## The window

- **Menus, shortcuts and Bus actions are one registry.** Every action has
  the same id in the menu bar, as a shortcut (Notepad++ conventions: see
  Help › Keyboard Shortcuts) and in `ced.action {id}`.
- **Tabs** show unsaved changes, and ◆ when another origin edited the
  document since you last looked at it.
- **The notice strip** keeps warnings, edits that could not be applied
  (re-insert them at the caret or dismiss them), and a document that lost
  its connection to the service (keep your copy or take the service's).
- **Find** (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H) runs in the service, so it searches the shared
  text, not a local copy.
- **Markdown and commit messages wrap**; code scrolls sideways.
- **Problems** (Ctrl+Shift+M) lists the document's diagnostics.
- View › Theme picks this window's scheme, style and mode.

## Bus

`ced.*` (schema `ced.v1`): `ping`, `info`, `open`, `new`, `tabs`, `focus`,
`state`, `type`, `select`, `action`, `actions`, `wait`, `layout`, `stats`,
`diagnostics`, `problems`, plus `app.describe` and `app.quit`; and the
toolkit drive verbs (`ced.ui.*`, `ced.window`, `ced.window.state`; see
[driving an app](../docs/drive.md)). A Bus caller's edits carry its own
origin (`agent:ced.<caller>`), so they show as an agent's, and its undo is
its own.

## Source

- `crates/documents`: the engine, with no UI toolkit. Open documents (one
  tab per buffer of the edit service, each a mirror with its editing model,
  highlighting and diagnostics), every action, the `ced.*` verbs and their
  waiters, reconnects and reattaches, the session.
- `src/`: the shell. The Bus thread, `ced --headless`, and the egui window
  around the shared [editor](../editor/README.md) text view.

The source is [`apps/ced`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/apps/ced).

## Tests

`cargo test -p documents -p ced`: the engine's unit and golden verb-fixture
tests, and `tests/window.rs`, which runs the real window against the fake
edit service in-process (no Bus): typing reaches the service, and two
offscreen snapshots. Regenerate them with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` and look at
them before committing.

## Not yet

- Macros and the Output panel's content.
- Linting Mix files on save (the Problems panel shows diagnostics other
  tools send with `ced.diagnostics`).
- Paste from the menu asks the platform for the clipboard; the primary
  selection (middle click) is the compositor's, not ced's.

<!-- page: https://mixos.dev/citizen/ (source: https://mixos.dev/citizen/README.md) -->

# citizen

An app's supervised native Bus connection, shared by the MixOS apps
(BusViewer, [Prefs](../prefs/README.md)). Headless: no UI dependency.

- `start(app, service, url)`: register as `service` and receive
  `Delivery`s: commands for the app, `Changed` (service registration),
  `Theme`, `Connected` and `Disconnected`.
- `Handle`: `raw`/`call` other services (30 s), or `raw_within` with a
  longer limit for work that legitimately runs long; `reply` once to each
  command; `quit`, which answers every accepted command
  (`BUSY: <app> is closing`) before the connection closes; `wait_done`.
- `probe`/`forward`: single-instance launch through `<app>.ping` and
  `<app>.show`; `noded_url()`: the broker this session uses.
- `show(handle, comp, app_id)`: restore and focus this process's window
  through [compd](../compd/README.md).
- With the `testing` feature: `Handle::sink()`, a handle with no connection
  that logs its calls, replies and quit.

Promoted from BusViewer's engine when Prefs became its second owner (see
[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/AGENTS.md) §2.2). Test
with `cargo test -p citizen`.

The source is [`libs/citizen`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/libs/citizen).

<!-- page: https://mixos.dev/compd/ (source: https://mixos.dev/compd/README.md) -->

# compd

The MixOS Wayland compositor.

compd owns KMS scanout, the GLES renderer and one shared wgpu device, its
own egui surfaces (capture overlays, notifications, the Mix Scenes shell),
the Xwayland window manager, frame pacing, fractional scale, input devices
and capture. On top of that sits the MixOS policy layer: the agent seat,
the `comp` Bus service (verbs, topics and the props tree), the frame and
presentation ledgers, panel holders and hot corners, and strict idle
discipline (no frames on a static screen).

Bevy, when enabled, may render effects on the shared wgpu device. It never
owns the frame loop, scheduling, compositing or protocol handling.

## Settings at startup

Quoin prepares cached or embedded settings while its existing Bus
supervisor registers. Its persistent cache is service-owned under the
configured variable data directory at `compd/cache/settings`; all
validation and filesystem work runs on the scene host's Bus worker
(`scene-host` `lane`). `shell.props.get` exposes `settings` and
`settings_cache` evidence. A cache persistence receipt must match the
current applied identity before it describes that presentation. Transport
outages and terminal registration refusal preserve usable appearance. Only
explicit initial refusal permits the configured scene service override; an
established shell identity never switches names. Shutdown drains the newest
activated capture and closes the worker under one two-second budget with a
bounded completion margin. Timeouts report failure without claiming
persistence.

The settings come from [settingsd](../settingsd/README.md) through the
[settings](../settings/README.md) library.

## Toast scenes

A scene with `window: {"kind":"toast","w":360,"h":120}` uses a
separate, pointer-interactive toast seat. It never takes keyboard focus,
including on click or with an authored autofocus field. It draws above
windows and edge panels, below the dialog and session lock.

The draft intent verbs are `shell.toast.show {scene, output?, h?}` and
`shell.toast.hide {scene}`. Both reply `{scene, visible, applied:true}`.
Scenes load hidden; show reserves the one toast seat and hide releases it.
A different scene's show returns rc 10 `TOAST_BUSY` with
`holder:{scene, owner}`. Unknown scenes return `NOT_FOUND`, other mount
kinds `NOT_TOAST`, and a nonnumeric height `INVALID_HEIGHT`.

The output defaults to the selected output, as for dialogs. Width clamps
to 240–2048 logical px and height to 60–2048 (defaults 360×120). A show can
override height; showing the same scene again resizes it, and omitting
height preserves its current override. Reload updates the authored geometry
and keeps visibility; changing kind requires an unload first.

Placement is top right, 12 logical px inside the usable area left by
layer-shell exclusive zones and docked scene panels. The drawn size fits
inside that area on small outputs. Chrome defaults to false; `chrome:true`
adds a title frame and a close button that hides the toast.

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/` | the `compd` binary: CLI, event loop, Bus and scene wiring |
| `crates/` | compd's private crates (engine, protocols, policy, backends) |
| `layers.conf.mix` | the private crates' dependency order, checked by `tools/layering_gate.mix` |
| `tests/` | integration tests |

The source is
[`services/compd`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/services/compd).
The desktop-tier gates that run compd nested or on hardware live in
[`tests/desktop/`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/tests/desktop)
at the repository root.

## Build

```
cargo build --profile release-fast -p compd                     # nested backend
cargo build --profile release-fast -p compd --no-default-features \
    --features backend-native                                   # KMS backend
cargo build --profile release-fast -p compd --features backend-all   # both
```

`capture-ffmpeg` adds hardware video capture through libav; the default
build links no FFmpeg.

`desktop-dbus` explicitly enables the optional desktop compatibility
adapters. The default native session has no D-Bus client or portal
dependency. It passes environment directly to children; delegated cgroup
placement before exec and `cgroup.kill` provide complete cleanup when
`MIXOS_CONTAIN_CHILDREN=1`.

## Run

Nested, inside another Wayland session:

```
compd --nested --socket wayland-compd --config-file=settings.json
```

On a VT, through the seat (libseat/seatd):

```
compd kms-live --device /dev/dri/card1 --connector HDMI-A-1 --scale 2.5
```

compd waits for its own VT to become active and never switches VT itself.
`--bus-service NAME` and `--scene-service NAME` override the Bus names
(default `comp`); `compd --help` lists every flag. Settings are read from
`--config-file`, else `~/.config/compd/settings.json`. Preferences are read
from `preferences.json` beside it.

`cursor_sensitivity` in `preferences.json` is a speed multiplier on top of
the output scale: compd multiplies each relative pointer delta by both, so
`1.0` moves the cursor at the same logical speed at every scale. Clients
asking for relative motion get the raw deltas.

## Session activity

`comp.session.get {}` is a draft query returning
`{"version":1,"active":true,"vt":3,"since_ms":1792108800123}`. `active`
describes this compositor's libseat session, including while paused after a
console VT switch. `since_ms` is Unix milliseconds at the last transition,
or at compd's Bus startup before the first transition.

Topic `<service>.session.changed` (normally `comp.session.changed`) publishes
`{"version":1,"active":false,"vt":3,"since_ms":1792108800456,"event_seq":42}`
once at startup and once on each pause or resume. It uses the shared
observation sequence, outbox and gap reporting. The publisher runs on its
own Bus worker, so pause events do not wait for rendering or resumption.
Subscribe before querying to establish the current state without polling;
on an observation gap, query again. Across desks, the most recent
`active:true` transition identifies the desk the human is viewing.

The session unit supplies `MIXOS_VT=%i`. compd reads it once when starting
its Bus service; `vt` is a u32 or `null` when the variable is absent or
cannot be parsed. A nested compositor with no supplied VT reports `null`.
The VT is never inferred from a runtime path or display name.

## Workspaces

Every output has a current workspace; windows belong to one. Verbs on the
`comp` service:

| Verb | Arguments | Reply |
|---|---|---|
| `comp.workspaces.list` | none | `{count, current, o_<key>: {current}, list: [{index, windows, name}]}`, the same object as `comp.props.get {path: "workspaces"}`; `name` is null when unnamed |
| `comp.workspace.switch` | `{index, output?, wrap?}` | `{output, from, to}` |
| `comp.window.send_to_workspace` | `{id, generation, index, follow?}` | the window |
| `comp.workspaces.set_count` | `{count: 1..=16, persist?}` | `{from, count, persisted?, persist_error?}` |
| `comp.workspace.rename` | `{index, name, persist?}` | `{index, name, previous, persisted?}` |

`index` is 1-based; switch and send also take `"next"` and `"prev"`.
Shrinking the count moves every window above it to the last workspace and
drops the removed workspaces' names. A name is trimmed, at most 64
characters, with no control characters; `""` clears it. `persist` defaults
to true: the count and the names are written to `preferences.json`
(`workspaces_count`, `workspace_names`) and compd starts with them. If the
file cannot be written, the change still applies and the reply has
`persisted: false` and `persist_error`. A session lock refuses every
workspace change and hides the names (and window counts) from readers.

Topic `comp.workspace.changed` (`<service>.workspace.changed`) carries
`{version: 1, count, current, outputs: {o_<key>: current}, names, event_seq}`
whenever the count, a current workspace or a name changes. `names` has one
entry per workspace, null when unnamed. Window counts are not in it;
`comp.props.changed` on `workspaces.list` carries them. The two topics are
sequenced separately, so a subscriber may see one before the other.

## Test

```
cargo test --workspace
mix tests/desktop/nested_smoke.mix --help
mix tests/desktop/parity_suite.mix --help
```

<!-- page: https://mixos.dev/config/ (source: https://mixos.dev/config/README.md) -->

# config

Where MixOS keeps its files, and how a `*.conf.mix` file is read.

- `config::path(Dir::Etc | Var | Run | Share)`: one rule for every
  directory. A `MIXOS_ETC` / `MIXOS_VAR` / `MIXOS_RUN` / `MIXOS_SHARE`
  override wins; else `$MIXOS/etc`, `/var`, `/run` when a root is set; else
  the XDG directory for a user (`~/.config/mixos`, `~/.local/share/mixos`,
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/mixos`) or the system directory for root (`/etc/mixos`,
  `/var/lib/mixos`, `/run/mixos`). `Share` is installed read-only data at
  `/opt/mixos/share` whatever the root or user. Resolved once per process
  and cached; `Dirs::resolve(&Environment)` applies the rule to explicit
  inputs for tests.
- `config::parse` / `config::parse_file` and `Value`, `Map`, `Error`,
  `ErrorKind`: the [strict](../strict/README.md) crate's strict-data
  loader, re-exported so a config reader needs one dependency. Typed
  loading is `strict::from_file`.

No dependency on the Mix language. Test with `cargo test -p config`.

The source is [`libs/config`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/libs/config).

## Application directories

`AppDirs` shares the existing Ced/Dopus per-application root, config, state
and cache rules. First absolute root wins: `MIXOS_APP_HOME`, then
`MIXOS_APPS_HOME/<component>`, `MIXOS_VAR/apps/<component>` (or
`MIXOS/var/apps/<component>`), `XDG_STATE_HOME/mixos/apps/<component>`,
then `HOME/.local/state/mixos/apps/<component>`. An invalid component or
absent absolute root returns `None`. Resolution performs no I/O. App-owned
filenames stay in their owners; this promotion preserves existing paths and
lets other native settings consumers use the same isolated cache policy.
`resolve_with` injects inputs for tests without mutating process
environment.

## Atomic directories

`atomic::open_directory` refuses symlinks in every component.
`atomic::create_directory` uses the same held-descriptor walk and provisions
missing components with mode 0700. It validates the entire absolute path
before creation, refuses parent traversal and leaves existing permissions
unchanged.

<!-- page: https://mixos.dev/davproto/ (source: https://mixos.dev/davproto/README.md) -->

# davproto

CalDAV and CardDAV codecs: the wire-format side of a DAV server or client,
with no transport and no storage.

- `ical`: JSCalendar (RFC 8984) to iCalendar VEVENT (RFC 5545), and the
  reverse mapping for a DAV PUT. A verbatim iCalendar body is kept under a
  data key so a GET returns it unchanged.
- `vcard`: JSContact (RFC 9553) to vCard 4.0 (RFC 6350), with the same
  verbatim round-trip.
- `etag`: strong ETags, a BLAKE3 hash of the content, so an ETag changes
  exactly when the content does.

The crate is a pure library. It does not open sockets, read files or touch
a database. Callers (maild's DAV server, a future DAV client) own those.

The source is [`libs/davproto`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/libs/davproto).

## Test

Run the unit tests on a build worker, not locally:

    cargo test -p davproto --locked
    cargo clippy -p davproto --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo fmt -p davproto -- --check

<!-- page: https://mixos.dev/design/ (source: https://mixos.dev/design/README.md) -->

# design

The MixOS design-token system. A design source is a strict-data document
(`theme.conf.mix`) holding OKLCH colour primitives, metrics, type scales,
semantic text pairs and the button family's mapping rules, plus modifier
blocks per scheme and mode. The compiler flattens it for one
`DesignContext` (scheme, mode, contrast, optional app) into a resolved
design: gamut-mapped colours with WCAG contrast checked, resolved metrics
and typography, and a total button table keyed by variant, size,
interaction and focus. Every failure is a stable, source-addressed
diagnostic.

The crate is headless and has no renderer dependency. Its only
dependencies are [strict](../strict/README.md) (the source format) and
`serde`.

- `parse_design_source` / `parse_legacy_v0_source` read a source; the
  embedded default is `EMBEDDED_DEFAULT_SOURCE`.
- `compile_design` produces a `DesignCompileResult`; `apply_compiled_design`
  stamps a revision onto an accepted candidate.
- `Scheme`, `Mode`, `Contrast` are the closed selection axes;
  `active_typography` reads a typography role with embedded defaults.
- The default selection, used when nothing chooses a theme, is studio,
  dark. `DesignContext::revision_one()` is revision one's ocean, light,
  which the v0 equivalence gate and the revision-one parity tests pin.

Build and test with `cargo test -p design`.

The source is [`libs/design`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/tree/main/libs/design).
