# Changelog

> Mirrored from [`cli/mix-shell/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/cli/mix-shell/CHANGELOG.md), where releases update it. The component's page is [mix-shell](README.md). This page describes the current `main` branch of MixOS.

## 0.116.0

### Added

- Released with mix 0.116.0: the remote mix binary for `ssh_mix` and the
  other remote-mix builtins comes from the `mix_bin` option, else
  `MIX_REMOTE_BIN`, else `/opt/cosmix/bin/mix` (`mix man remote`).

## 0.115.0

### Added

- Released with mix 0.115.0: `unix_connect()` opens a local unix-domain
  stream socket, with NUL-terminated frames for Varlink and hostd
  (`mix man system`).

## 0.114.0

### Changed

- Usage statistics are an append-only JSONL store. A run's exit appends one
  record to `runs/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` with a single write and does nothing
  else, so recording costs nothing measurable: `mix -c 1` went from 151 ms
  to 52 ms on a host with a busy history, the same as with stats off. Raw
  day files are never rewritten; `cache/` holds disposable per-day
  aggregates checked against the exact raw file; reports filter by each
  bucket's own date. `mix stats query` runs SQL over the old `mix.db` tables
  built in memory, so on a large history it now takes about a second.
- `clear` and `reset` append an operation anchored to storage positions, not
  a clock, under `ops.lock`. They refuse while the old weekly documents
  (`current.json`, `YYYY-WNN.json`) exist; those are read in place, never
  moved, and their `stats.lock` is never taken, so an older mix still writing
  them keeps working. `mix man stats` documents the store.

### Fixed

- A session task no longer inherits file descriptors the shell itself
  inherited without close-on-exec.

## 0.113.1

### Fixed

- Built on mix 0.113.1: `on dopus-test.command.executed` (a hyphenated
  handler name) now fires; before, it parsed and never did. `mix man bus`
  documents it.

## 0.113.0

### Added

- Built on mix 0.113.0 with the `mime` feature: `mime_type()` names a
  file's type as the desktop does. `mix man io` documents it.

## 0.112.1

### Fixed

- Built on mix 0.112.1: SIGTERM and Ctrl-C end a blocking `tcp_accept`,
  `tcp_recv`, `tcp_recv_line` or `ws_recv` at once, `tcp_send` takes a
  whole-send `{timeout}` (`TCP_SEND_TIMEOUT`), and receives serve buffered
  data first while traffic that delivers nothing counts against the
  deadline. `mix man system` documents them.

## 0.112.0

### Added

- Built on mix 0.112.0: server-side TCP (`tcp_listen`, `tcp_accept`,
  `tcp_local_addr`, `tcp_on` on a listener) and `on @.verb`, which registers
  a handler under the `--serve` name so one generic script serves any
  instance. `mix man serve` and `mix man system` document both.

### Fixed

- The serve reload lifecycle test's TERM-ignoring fixture creates the trace
  file itself. The citizen spawned it before the first trace line existed,
  so a fast start panicked on open and the grace test timed out.

## 0.111.0

### Fixed

- An interrupted run exits with status 130 (128+SIGINT) derived from the signal
  actually received, never from error text: an ordinary error whose message
  mentions `interrupted` now fails with its own diagnostic instead of exiting 0.
- SIGINT/SIGTERM are honoured during `--serve` startup (stalled broker
  registration, CPU-bound preludes, reloads) and during `-c`, script and
  `.mixrc` prelude loading. A caught interrupt cannot end in success, and
  `--result-fd` always reports it as an error frame.
- `script_path()` is resolved before the prelude runs in script and serve modes.

## 0.109.4

Initial MixOS shell transplant. Language semantics retain the source version.
Application transport is native ABP through noded. Runtime directories use the
shared config rule; installed manuals are available offline. Cross-process
native-session handoff bytes retain the frozen compatibility contract.

# noded changes

> Mirrored from [`services/noded/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/services/noded/CHANGELOG.md), where releases update it. The component's page is [noded](README.md). This page describes the current `main` branch of MixOS.

## 0.18.3

Add a structured rejection body to the different-channel `noded.register`
collision refusal: `{"schema": "noded.registration-rejection.v1",
"error_code": "NAME_TAKEN", "message": …}` alongside the unchanged `rc=10`
reply and `error` header. The body is additive only — ABP framing, return
codes, admission refusals and session transcript bytes are untouched — and
lets clients classify a collision without matching diagnostic text. The bus
client decodes it through a bounded typed envelope whose classification is
pinned by noded and bus tests.

## 0.18.2

Transplant the native broker, session authority and mesh routing to the MixOS
workspace. Preserve ABP verbs, admission domains and session transcript bytes.
Use strict MixOS configuration and owned shutdown signalling.

# settings contract changes

> Mirrored from [`libs/settings/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/libs/settings/CHANGELOG.md), where releases update it. The component's page is [settings](README.md). This page describes the current `main` branch of MixOS.

## 0.7.0

Additive, store format unchanged (3):

- `Desktop.terminal` (`terminal::Terminal`): the term's preferences under
  `terminal.*` (font family/size/weight, padding, scrollback lines, scroll
  speed, border width, cursor shape/blink, focus ring/strength, copy on
  select, `TERM`). Every default reproduces the term before the group
  existed except padding (8 px instead of 1 px) and the focus ring: its
  default, `accent` at strength 0.25, draws the focused pane's border as the
  card border moved a quarter toward the theme accent, where the term drew
  it halfway before. That change is intentional (a subtler tinted ring);
  `neutral` remains available, and `accent` with strength 0.5
  gives the old look. Omitted at its defaults (and each value within it), so older
  profiles keep their seals. It does not touch `Effective`, as `keymaps`
  does not. A profile that sets any of it will not load in a 0.6.0 build:
  reset `terminal` first.
- `Summary.terminal` and `Followed::Look.terminal` carry it to followers.
- `settings.describe` lists each `terminal.*` field with its range and
  default; `terminal` alone resets or replaces the whole group.
- `terminal: null` resets the whole terminal group, as advertised.
- Correct the scroll speed unit: rows per wheel line, scaled by speed/40;
  touchpad travel counts in cell heights at that scale. Default 40 keeps
  the existing one-row-per-wheel-line behaviour; it is not a pixel distance.

## 0.6.0

Additive, store format 3 ([decision](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/docs/docs/decisions/2026-10-14-session-icon-stroke-and-type.md)):

- `Appearance` and `Effective` gain four optional session choices:
  `icon_stroke` (1.0 to 3.0 in quarter steps), `font_family`,
  `font_weight` (100 to 900 in steps of 100) and `mono_family`. Each is
  omitted when unset, so profiles without them keep their digests.
- `ChangePlan`: `icon_stroke` is a paint change; the font choices are
  resource and text changes.
- `CompactEffective` carries the same fields.
- The store writes format 3. A format-2 build refuses a profile that sets
  any of them; reset them first with `settings.reset` or a null value.

Rust API change: `Followed::Look.appearance` is now `Box<Appearance>` to keep
follower events compact as font settings grow. Borrowed callers use deref
coercion; callers that take ownership unwrap with `*appearance`.

## 0.5.0

Authority verbs 0.3.0 (additive): snapshot schema 2
([decision](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/docs/docs/decisions/2026-10-11-settings-snapshot-schema-2.md)).

- `compact`: `CompactSnapshot` (schema 2) sends each distinct design
  projection once under `designs`, keyed by digest; each context's `design`
  names one. `encode` builds it; `decode` reads schema 1 or 2 into the same
  in-memory `Snapshot`, so consumers, reducer, cache and effective digests
  are unchanged. A dangling or unnamed design is refused.
- `compact_topic(profile)` / `COMPACT_TOPIC_PREFIX`: the retained schema 2
  topic, `settingsd.desktop.compact.<profile>`, published between the
  schema 1 topic and the summary.
- **Breaking:** `ReadRequest.schema` (1 by default and never serialised;
  2 for the compact form) on `settings.get` and `settings.appearance.get`.
  Another schema is refused with `unsupported_schema`.
- `native` follows the compact topic and reads schema 2. Consumers on the
  schema 1 topic are not affected.
- `describe()` lists the snapshot schemas and the compact topic.

## 0.4.0

Authority verbs 0.2.0 (additive), snapshot schema still 1
([decision](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/docs/docs/decisions/2026-10-11-settings-summary-reads.md)):

- `Summary` (schema 1): binding, incarnation, revision, design revision,
  source digest, appearance names and `custom_source`; never projections or
  a custom source. `summary_topic(profile)` /
  `SUMMARY_TOPIC_PREFIX` name its retained topic,
  `settingsd.desktop.summary.<profile>`, published beside the snapshot topic.
- `ReadRequest.view` (`View::Full`, the default and never serialised, or
  `View::Summary`) selects `settings.get`'s answer.
- `follow::Follower` subscribes to the summary topic and reads the summary
  view. **Breaking:** `Followed::Look` gains `custom_source`, and its
  `appearance.source` is always `None`.
- `describe()` lists the read views and both topics.

The cache interpretation includes the library version, so caches written by
0.3.x fall back visibly once.

## 0.3.5

Add the appearance keys `appearance.style` (null, the default, takes the
scheme's own style; else plain, pro, studio or classic),
`appearance.decorations` (csd, the default, or ssd) and
`appearance.caption_side` (right, the default, or left). They resolve into
every effective context; a style change is a paint and layout change and a
decorations or caption-side change a layout change. Older desktops and
snapshots load with the defaults. Authority verbs/schema remain 0.1.0/1.

## 0.3.4

Expose the public snapshot identity of an activated cache capture so hosts can
report fenced persistence receipts without copying its projection or private
producer serial. Authority verbs/schema remain 0.1.0/1. The cache interpretation
includes the library version; older caches fall back visibly without affecting
authority history.

## 0.3.3

Add immutable cache targets for borrowed workers, capture deduplication and
producer-fenced writer opening. Add lazy persistent fallback loading after
retained resource validation, preserving load diagnostics when embedded works.
Authority verbs/schema remain 0.1.0/1. Older presentation caches are rejected
because the cache interpretation includes this library version.

## 0.3.2

Expose shared consumer evidence with separate accepted and applied identities,
connection generation, confirmation, presentation kind and faults. Readback
never claims frame presentation or broker participant registration. Authority
verbs and snapshot schema remain 0.1.0 and 1.

## 0.3.1

Split authenticated native delivery decoding from UI consumer handling, retaining
binding/generation fences in the decoded value. Add shared session binding and
capture identity predicates for coalesced resource scheduling. Authority wire
contract/schema remain 0.1.0/1. The cache interpretation includes this crate's
version, so older local presentation caches are rejected and embedded defaults
remain available; authority persistence is unaffected.

## 0.3.0

Add shared retained/cache/embedded fallback preparation with host resource
validation, immutable stage fencing and explicit presentation labels. Persisted
data never seeds authority ordering or mutation fences. Optional cache I/O
uses bounded no-follow directory-relative reads and atomic replacement, with
schema/target/capability/digest checks plus complete projection recompilation.
Applied-generation captures and one locked serial writer reject stale saves;
ambiguous post-rename failure remains visible. Exact JSON float round trips
preserve compiler projection comparison. The authority wire/schema stay
0.1.0/1. Real resource loading, GUI/first-map timing and artifact integration
remain pending.
Keep fallback preparation/activation faults separate from authority/current
resource faults, and detect unsupported cache headers before strict body parsing.

## 0.2.0

Add transport-neutral consumer and render-domain change plan, with an optional
native executor over an app-owned supervised connection. Bound work/buffering,
coalesce queue-loss recovery, fence connection/consumer/renderer completions,
and advance unchanged render evidence without a redraw. Retired confirmation
candidates are deduplicated within a bounded history. No owned runtime or
renderer dependency. Authority wire contract/schema remain 0.1.0/1.
Use canonical app/shell constructors, captured read baselines/tickets and one
absolute recovery deadline. Malformed-event storms cannot bypass the deadline;
same-incarnation rollback is distinct from a read racing a newer publication.
DTO additions require explicit render/evidence classification at compile time.
Persisted fallback cache, artifact/resource preparation and GUI activation are
still pending; this API does not advertise their completion.

## 0.1.0

Initial binding/revision/receipt/snapshot types, independent design read
projection, validated batch vocabulary and ordering/work-ticket reducer.
Renderer transport/bootstrap adapters remain pending.
Before initial release: report confirmed same-revision contradictions and
validate authored app enum values before accessibility precedence.

# Terminal Bus contract

> Mirrored from [`apps/term/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/markc/mixos/blob/main/apps/term/CHANGELOG.md), where releases update it. The component's page is [term](README.md). This page describes the current `main` branch of MixOS.

## 0.4.0

The window is egui on wgpu, its grid drawn on the GPU by `term-render`.
The terminal's own verbs (`term.session`, `term.tabs`, `term.tab.*`,
`term.panes`, `term.pane.*`, `term.snapshot`, `term.scroll`, `term.type`,
`term.props.watch`, INFO and HELP) are unchanged.

Added: `term.commands` and `term.execute` (every window action by command
id), `app.describe`, the toolkit drive verbs (`term.ui.*`, `term.window`,
`term.window.state`), and `term.command.executed`, published for every
command run with how it was reached.

Alt is Meta: ESC before the key (readline's Alt+b/f/., Alt+Backspace,
Alt+Enter), and Alt+cursor keys send xterm's CSI 1;3 sequences.
Ctrl+[ and the other control punctuation send their control codes.

Program (OSC) titles now reach the tab strip without a `term.props.watch`
watcher. Right Shift with Left/Right no longer changes tab: right-hand
modifier chords are the person's own keys on MixOS.

## 0.3.5

Shared the native application bootstrap and task worker. PTY ownership
and ordered teardown stay in the terminal. The native session contract is
unchanged.

## 0.3.4

The terminal frontend and native session verbs entered the tree. The
cross-process session constants and the child-only descriptor handoff keep
their bytes.

# Desktop components

The components a MixOS desktop installs, generated from each component's declared
install profiles. A component in more than one profile is listed on each page. Every
component, with its kind and source, is in the [component index](components.md); see also
the [server](server.md) list. This page describes the current `main` branch of MixOS.

## Core components

On every MixOS system.

- [monitord](../monitord/README.md) (service): How monitord samples a host's CPU, memory, disks, network and processes, keeps history in memory and SQLite, and answers read verbs on the Bus, so any node's load can be read from anywhere on the…

## Desktop components

- [monitor](../monitor/README.md) (app): Monitor is the MixOS task manager, showing the processes and performance that monitord reports for this node or any node on the mesh, with End task and Kill for this node's processes.

## Unclassified

Apps, services and command-line components that do not declare install profiles
yet. They are listed on both this page and the server page until they do.

- [backdrop](../backdrop/README.md) (app): The MixOS desktop background — drawn by its own program on the compositor's background layer, on every output, at native and fractional scale.
- [bridged](../bridged/README.md) (service): How bridged puts an external application with a line-delimited JSON control channel on the Bus, one instance per application, and what that exposes.
- [busviewer](../busviewer/README.md) (app): BusViewer is the MixOS desktop app that lists the services and verbs on this node's Bus, shows each verb's description and the mesh peers, and calls one verb once with a JSON body.
- [ced](../ced/README.md) (app): The MixOS Editor, a desktop text editor over the edit Bus service, where people and agents edit the same document at once and see each other's carets, selections and changes live.
- [compd](../compd/README.md) (service): The MixOS Wayland compositor, which owns scanout, rendering, input and capture, and serves the comp Bus service with its workspaces, verbs, topics and props tree.
- [dopus](../dopus/README.md) (app): MixOS's twin-pane file manager — two folder trees side by side, Places and Properties sidebars, drag and drop between panes, menus and keys for every action, and a Bus surface for agents that reads…
- [editd](../editd/README.md) (service): The edit service, which holds shared text buffers that people and agents edit together, with revision checks, per-origin undo, anchors, atomic save, external-change detection and recovery.
- [email](../email/README.md) (app)
- [hostd](../hostd/README.md) (service): How hostd answers questions about the host and carries out privileged host changes through closed, typed verbs behind standing grants, receipts and rollback, so agents never need sudo.
- [mix-shell](../mix-shell/README.md) (cli): The Mix shell library, holding the interactive line editor, the command classifier, the native-session bootstrap and the Bus citizen runtime that the mix binary runs.
- [noded](../noded/README.md) (service): The MixOS Bus broker, which handles service registration, discovery, routing, subscriptions, authenticated local session grants and mesh peering between nodes.
- [notifyd](../notifyd/README.md) (service): How notifyd keeps the desk's notifications, shows them as toasts and in the Notifications page, and tells an agent or app which button the human pressed.
- [portald](../portald/README.md) (service): How portald serves the XDG Settings portal on the session bus, where the appearance values come from, and how applications and agents read them.
- [prefs](../prefs/README.md) (app): MixOS's preferences window — a sidebar of editors: Applications follows, installs, updates, rolls back and removes upstream releases; Appearance sets the session's colour scheme, style, mode,…
- [releasesd](../releasesd/README.md) (service): How releasesd follows upstream application releases on GitHub and installs their Linux builds per user, verified, with rollback, from the command line or the Bus.
- [screenshot](../screenshot/README.md) (app): MixOS's screenshot app — Print Screen for a region, Shift+Print for the screen, Alt+Print for a window; arrows, boxes, pens, highlighter, text, numbered markers, crop and redaction that stay…
- [settingsd](../settingsd/README.md) (service): The headless desktop settings authority, the one writer for a session profile's settings, with durable receipts and retained change publication on the Bus.
- [system](../system/README.md) (cli): The system binary, mix, which is the Mix shell and every headless MixOS daemon in one file, choosing its personality from the name it is started under.
- [term](../term/README.md) (app): The MixOS terminal, with tabs, split panes and a GPU-drawn grid, driven by the session settings and fully scriptable over the Bus.

# Server components

The components a MixOS server installs, generated from each component's declared
install profiles. A component in more than one profile is listed on each page. Every
component, with its kind and source, is in the [component index](components.md); see also
the [desktop](desktop.md) list. This page describes the current `main` branch of MixOS.

## Core components

On every MixOS system.

- [monitord](../monitord/README.md) (service): How monitord samples a host's CPU, memory, disks, network and processes, keeps history in memory and SQLite, and answers read verbs on the Bus, so any node's load can be read from anywhere on the…

## Server components

None yet.

## Unclassified

Apps, services and command-line components that do not declare install profiles
yet. They are listed on both this page and the desktop page until they do.

- [backdrop](../backdrop/README.md) (app): The MixOS desktop background — drawn by its own program on the compositor's background layer, on every output, at native and fractional scale.
- [bridged](../bridged/README.md) (service): How bridged puts an external application with a line-delimited JSON control channel on the Bus, one instance per application, and what that exposes.
- [busviewer](../busviewer/README.md) (app): BusViewer is the MixOS desktop app that lists the services and verbs on this node's Bus, shows each verb's description and the mesh peers, and calls one verb once with a JSON body.
- [ced](../ced/README.md) (app): The MixOS Editor, a desktop text editor over the edit Bus service, where people and agents edit the same document at once and see each other's carets, selections and changes live.
- [compd](../compd/README.md) (service): The MixOS Wayland compositor, which owns scanout, rendering, input and capture, and serves the comp Bus service with its workspaces, verbs, topics and props tree.
- [dopus](../dopus/README.md) (app): MixOS's twin-pane file manager — two folder trees side by side, Places and Properties sidebars, drag and drop between panes, menus and keys for every action, and a Bus surface for agents that reads…
- [editd](../editd/README.md) (service): The edit service, which holds shared text buffers that people and agents edit together, with revision checks, per-origin undo, anchors, atomic save, external-change detection and recovery.
- [email](../email/README.md) (app)
- [hostd](../hostd/README.md) (service): How hostd answers questions about the host and carries out privileged host changes through closed, typed verbs behind standing grants, receipts and rollback, so agents never need sudo.
- [mix-shell](../mix-shell/README.md) (cli): The Mix shell library, holding the interactive line editor, the command classifier, the native-session bootstrap and the Bus citizen runtime that the mix binary runs.
- [noded](../noded/README.md) (service): The MixOS Bus broker, which handles service registration, discovery, routing, subscriptions, authenticated local session grants and mesh peering between nodes.
- [notifyd](../notifyd/README.md) (service): How notifyd keeps the desk's notifications, shows them as toasts and in the Notifications page, and tells an agent or app which button the human pressed.
- [portald](../portald/README.md) (service): How portald serves the XDG Settings portal on the session bus, where the appearance values come from, and how applications and agents read them.
- [prefs](../prefs/README.md) (app): MixOS's preferences window — a sidebar of editors: Applications follows, installs, updates, rolls back and removes upstream releases; Appearance sets the session's colour scheme, style, mode,…
- [releasesd](../releasesd/README.md) (service): How releasesd follows upstream application releases on GitHub and installs their Linux builds per user, verified, with rollback, from the command line or the Bus.
- [screenshot](../screenshot/README.md) (app): MixOS's screenshot app — Print Screen for a region, Shift+Print for the screen, Alt+Print for a window; arrows, boxes, pens, highlighter, text, numbered markers, crop and redaction that stay…
- [settingsd](../settingsd/README.md) (service): The headless desktop settings authority, the one writer for a session profile's settings, with durable receipts and retained change publication on the Bus.
- [system](../system/README.md) (cli): The system binary, mix, which is the Mix shell and every headless MixOS daemon in one file, choosing its personality from the name it is started under.
- [term](../term/README.md) (app): The MixOS terminal, with tabs, split panes and a GPU-drawn grid, driven by the session settings and fully scriptable over the Bus.
